name: Suno
product: Text-to-music AI app that turns a prompt into a complete song in seconds.
pricing_model: Freemium with paid subscriptions; sources report 2M+ paying subscribers
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Aspiring Afrobeats, amapiano and gospel creators in Lagos, Accra, Nairobi and Johannesburg who want to prototype songs cheaply would pay for Pro credits if they could pay with mobile money instead of a card.
notes: Valued at $5.4B; about $300M ARR reported. Large company, so pitch should target payments/growth team. Ongoing label copyright litigation.

name: Tolan
hq_country: Not found (built by Portola; US-based team per press)
product: Voice-first AI companion character that helps users manage daily life, relationships, emotions and goals.
pricing_model: Subscription; App Store lists Lite at $11.99 and Plus at $24.99, with higher tiers; free tier planned
expansion_signal: Plans to launch a free tier to widen access to the app.
africa_use_case: Young urban professionals and parents in Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa seeking low-cost emotional support and life organisation could pay for the Lite tier in local currency.
founders: Quinten Farmer (CEO), Evan Goldschmidt, Ajay Mehta
notes: About 250,000 users; Khosla Ventures and Homebrew also participated. Upper tiers are too expensive for most African users, so pitch the Lite tier.

name: Sonilo
product: Generative audio tool that creates music and sound effects synced to the pacing and emotion of a creator's video.
expansion_signal: Funds earmarked for go-to-market expansion across creator and developer platforms and for growing music licensing.
africa_use_case: African TikTok, YouTube and Instagram creators who need licence-safe soundtracks for short videos would pay monthly if checkout accepted mobile money.
founders: Shawn Song (CEO), Alex Yin (CTO), Keli Li (COO); Trista Taylor is CMO
notes: Founded by ex-TikTok AI and music staff; Redpoint participated. Self-serve pricing not confirmed in sources.

name: Madverse Music Group
product: Music distribution, publishing and royalty platform for independent artists, releasing to major streaming services.
pricing_model: Subscription; Creator plan about Rs299/month, Professional about Rs3,999/year
expansion_signal: Announcement carried New Delhi and New York datelines, and the site runs country-specific pages for markets such as the US and Nepal.
africa_use_case: Independent Afrobeats, bongo flava and gqom artists who already pay for DistroKid-style distribution would pay a low-cost plan priced like Madverse's India tier via mobile money.
notes: Emerging-market pricing already fits African budgets. Amount of round not disclosed.

name: Wabi
product: Shared personal AI agent that builds personalised mini-apps for groups, couples and families.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Families and friend groups in African cities who coordinate on WhatsApp could pay for shared planners, budgets and chama-style group trackers built as Wabi mini-apps.
founders: Eugenia Kuyda (founder and CEO; also founded Replika)
notes: Valued at $1.25B; a16z, Forerunner and Amazon Alexa Fund participated. Monetisation not yet confirmed.

name: FLTRD
hq_country: Netherlands (inferred from Dutch user base; not explicitly stated)
product: Grocery-scanning nutrition app that scores how ultra-processed a product is and suggests healthier alternatives.
expansion_signal: Expanding to Belgium by end of 2026 and targeting 100 million users within five years across Europe.
africa_use_case: Health-conscious shoppers in South African and Kenyan supermarket chains (Shoprite, Pick n Pay, Carrefour Kenya) could pay for UPF scores once local product databases exist.
notes: Database covers seven European supermarkets; Africa needs a product-catalogue build. Also plans B2B licensing of PureScore.

name: Maple
product: Privacy-first AI chat and desktop agent running in encrypted enclaves so the company cannot read user data.
expansion_signal: None stated (plans a Series A in H1 2027).
africa_use_case: Journalists, lawyers, activists and developers in Africa who want private AI chat outside big-tech data collection could pay the $20 Pro plan in local currency.
notes: Draper Associates, Planetary VC and Epoch VC participated. Also sells a Teams plan. Founders came from the bitcoin-wallet space.

name: Stamina
product: Personalised triathlon training app that adapts swim, bike and run plans to fitness, goals and schedule.
lead_investors: Not found (backers include Greg Van Avermaet, Syndicate One, 100IN, Average Rob)
expansion_signal: Belgian coverage frames the raise as funding international growth.
africa_use_case: South African, Kenyan and Moroccan triathletes and endurance athletes preparing for Ironman races (e.g. Ironman South Africa) would pay for adaptive coaching.
notes: Niche but affluent audience; strongest in South Africa.

name: Quartz
product: Personal finance app that aggregates pensions, ISAs, savings and investments with an AI assistant giving personalised guidance.
expansion_signal: Launched in the UK with waitlist onboarding and gradual access expansion; team spread across London, Barcelona and Porto.
africa_use_case: Diaspora-linked and salaried African investors juggling local pensions, money-market funds and offshore accounts could pay for an AI wealth dashboard once local connectors exist.
founders: André Silva (CEO, ex-Revolut), Mateus Mesquita Alves (ex-N26)
notes: FCA-registered AISP; product is UK-specific today, so Africa fit depends on new data connectors.

name: Alta
product: AI styling app that builds an avatar from two selfies, digitises your wardrobe and renders outfit suggestions.
expansion_signal: Funding will expand both the consumer app and enterprise services for fashion brands.
africa_use_case: Fashion-forward Gen Z users in Lagos, Nairobi and Johannesburg, plus local designers, could pay for styling and virtual try-on features.
notes: Lifestyle app; Menlo Ventures and Aglaé Ventures participated. Brand partners include Gap and Rent the Runway.

name: Loora
product: AI English tutor app for conversational speaking practice with real-time feedback.
pricing_model: Subscription after one free lesson; third-party listing cites about $19.99/month
expansion_signal: Reports 15 million learners worldwide; Latin American coverage describes expansion from Argentina.
africa_use_case: Professionals and students in francophone and lusophone Africa (Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, DRC, Mozambique, Angola) who need business English for jobs would pay monthly.
notes: Edtech-adjacent individual productivity app. Strong Africa demand for English fluency; price point at upper bound.

name: Eevi
product: Voice-first AI language tutor that gets learners speaking through real-time conversation.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: African learners preparing to work or study in Europe (e.g. learning Dutch, German or French) would pay for conversation practice cheaper than tutors.
notes: Very early stage; amount undisclosed.

name: Matiks
product: Social mind-sports gaming app with competitive math, memory, logic and puzzle duels.
expansion_signal: Plans a US push and positions itself as a global mind-sports platform.
africa_use_case: Students and parents in Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana, where maths olympiads and exam prep are popular, could pay for premium competitive play.
founders: Sudhanshu Bhatia, Mohan Kumar, Sushant Timmapur
notes: About 300,000 daily players reported. Monetisation model not confirmed.

name: Notes.fm
product: Royalty collection, publishing administration and distribution platform for independent musicians.
lead_investors: Not found (backers include Zach Bryan, Benny Blanco, Ari Emanuel, Julie Greenwald, Sam Hendel)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Independent African artists who lose royalties from global streams and sync would pay to find and collect unclaimed money.
founders: Tim Luckow (co-founder, Stem co-founder); others not found
notes: Partnered with Musixmatch in November 2026 for synced lyrics.

name: Rocapine
product: AI-native venture studio building and scaling consumer wellness apps, including the cycle tracker Harmony.
expansion_signal: Aims to improve the lives of at least 40 million people within five years.
africa_use_case: Women in francophone Africa using cycle-tracking and wellbeing apps would pay for premium features if subscriptions accepted mobile money.
founders: Stanislas Marchand (CEO), Jean-Gabriel Boinot-Tramoni, Sammy Teillet
notes: Tests hundreds of app concepts a year and scales winners through performance marketing. One Cozzipay integration could cover a whole app portfolio.

name: Matters
product: AI-native consumer banking and personal finance app with an AI advisor for spending, saving and goals.
pricing_model: Subscription-based model (per tech.eu); price not found
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Salaried urban Africans who want AI budgeting and savings coaching on top of existing accounts could pay a small monthly fee.
notes: Bank model needs licensing per market, so Africa entry is slower.

name: A Vinyl Bar in Shibuya
product: Music software label releasing small interactive apps for playing with sound, vocals and AI music creation.
lead_investors: Not found (investors include Mantis VC, SV Angel, Boxgroup, Quiet Capital, Collaborative Fund)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Young African music fans and bedroom producers would buy playful vocal and remix apps through in-app purchases.
notes: Dawn Ostroff joined as adviser. Very early.

name: GasLab
product: Generative AI music app that attributes generated tracks to contributing musicians and pays them.
expansion_signal: Aims to grow into a worldwide platform for AI-generated music.
africa_use_case: African DJs and producers could pay to create with licensed artist models and earn attribution income from their own catalogues.
notes: Announced 15 Oct 2026 (tech.eu article dated 16 Oct).

name: URUNN
product: Running app with personalised 5K-to-marathon plans and coaching from elite athletes.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Runners in Kenya, Ethiopia, South Africa and Nigeria training for city marathons would pay for plans co-created by Somali-born Mo Farah.
founders: Sir Mo Farah, Adam Clarke, WithU (co-founders)
notes: Mo Farah's East African heritage gives a natural marketing angle.

name: Tomo
product: Text-message AI coach for habits, calorie tracking, budgeting and screen-time accountability.
pricing_model: Paid subscription; 10,000+ paying subscribers reported; price not found
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Self-improvement-minded young Africans could pay for accountability coaching, especially if Tomo ran on WhatsApp, the main messaging channel there.
founders: Justin Quan (co-founder and CEO); others not found
notes: Accel, Conviction and Pear VC participated. iMessage-first today.

name: SuperLiving
product: AI preventive-health app with wellness courses, regional content and a 24/7 AI companion for nutrition, movement, sleep and stress.
expansion_signal: Scaling across India's Tier II and III cities (domestic only).
africa_use_case: Mass-market users in secondary African cities facing rising diabetes and hypertension could afford a sub-$3 monthly AI health coach paid by mobile money.
notes: 73% of paid users are outside India's big metros, which proves the low-ARPU model Africa needs.

name: Mistlabs (Ambi)
product: Ambient AI assistant app for iPhone, Mac and Apple Watch that keeps context across devices and anticipates needs.
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Busy professionals and students with Apple devices in African capitals could pay for an always-on note and task assistant.
notes: Sources give 5 Oct (announcement) and 12 Oct (TechCrunch). Apple-only and also funds a future wearable. Weaker fit for Android-heavy Africa.

name: Savi Security
product: Family app that uses behavioural AI to screen calls, messages and communications for AI-powered scams.
pricing_model: Subscription; $7.99/month or $62.99/year per family, unlimited members
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Families in Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa targeted by mobile-money and impersonation scams would pay a family plan to protect elderly relatives.
notes: Price point fits; would need local telco and scam pattern data.

name: Onix
product: Subscription app where users talk to AI versions of named health and wellness experts, trained only on their licensed work.
expansion_signal: Funding supports expert onboarding as Onix moves to public availability.
africa_use_case: African wellness, fitness and faith influencers could launch paid AI twins for their followers, who would subscribe in local currency.
founders: David Bennahum (co-founder and CEO); others not found
notes: Garage Capital and Ride Home Fund participated.

name: Orbits
product: Bit, an AI household assistant that handles family logistics from meal planning to home repairs.
expansion_signal: Funding supports the wider consumer launch of Bit.
africa_use_case: Dual-income middle-class households in African cities managing school runs, domestic staff and bills could pay for an AI chief of staff.
notes: Press release says $2.6M; BetaKit clarifies that is CAD (about $2M USD).

name: The Wellness Company (Tempo)
product: Tempo, an AI health companion app that combines sleep, recovery, activity, nutrition and bloodwork into personalised next steps.
lead_investors: Not found (Inforcapital lists BDC Capital for an earlier 2026 seed)
expansion_signal: None stated
africa_use_case: Wearable-owning fitness enthusiasts in South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria could pay for AI insights across their health data.
notes: Consolidating a portfolio of apps into Tempo.

name: Kyndred
product: Animated AI companion characters with real-time voice and persistent memory that also help with everyday tasks.
expansion_signal: Funds will go to customer growth and more AI characters.
africa_use_case: Young Android users in Africa looking for voice-based companionship and English conversation practice could pay small in-app subscriptions.
notes: Android app live; lead character is Maya. Very early.

name: Spill Games
product: AI-led studio making free-to-play casual, puzzle and hybrid-casual mobile games for a global audience.
pricing_model: Free-to-play with in-app purchases (per sources describing free-to-play titles)
expansion_signal: Builds games for a global audience; funds go to user acquisition and scaling live titles.
africa_use_case: Africa's large casual-gamer base on Android rarely converts to in-app purchases because of card barriers; mobile-money IAP checkout could unlock that spend.
notes: Centre Court Capital and PeerCapital participated.

name: Bold Games
product: Mobile studio making sort-puzzle games, starting with its debut title Market Match.
pricing_model: Not found (casual mobile game; IAP model typical but not confirmed)
lead_investors: Arcadia Gaming Partners, Makers Fund, e2vc
expansion_signal: Capital to accelerate development and global expansion of Market Match.
africa_use_case: Casual puzzle players across North and Sub-Saharan Africa could buy boosters and ad-free passes with mobile money.
notes: JIMCO also participated.

name: dubdub
product: Swipe-based trivia and puzzle feed that replaces scrolling with quizzes and mini-games across 20+ categories.
expansion_signal: Plans to build a broader interactive entertainment platform.
africa_use_case: Young African phone users who love football and Nollywood trivia could pay for premium packs and tournaments with mobile money.
notes: About 20,000 downloads; monetisation not confirmed, so this lead is weaker on criterion 2. Date taken from coverage published around 23 Oct 2026.

name: Rebel Audio
product: AI podcasting platform to record, edit, dub, publish and monetise podcasts in one place.
expansion_signal: Product includes AI translation and dubbing so creators can reach new language audiences; more funding expected within 90 days.
africa_use_case: Africa's fast-growing podcaster community (Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa) would pay the $15 tier to produce and dub shows into English, French or Swahili.
notes: Seed of $4.15M preceded the Series A; Mark Burnett is an adviser.

name: Sleep.ai
product: Sleep intelligence platform and app that measures sleep via phone sonar or wearables and gives personalised coaching.
pricing_model: Not found (sources describe partner APIs and a reimbursed German programme)
expansion_signal: Funding supports expansion in Germany and other markets plus new partner integrations.
africa_use_case: Shift workers and stressed urban professionals in Africa with only a smartphone could pay for contactless sleep tracking and coaching.
notes: Formerly SleepScore Labs. Business has shifted toward B2B/insurer channels, so the self-serve consumer offer is unconfirmed. MobiHealthNews lists the round as $5.5M.
